Methodology & sources

This briefing uses only the supplied CSV. The 15-country sample is not the entire world. Findings describe this sample, and rankings are not global rankings. Missing observations are shown as unavailable and excluded from calculations that need them.

Prices, periods & units

Business electricity prices are retail rates, not specific industrial tariffs or total energy costs. The stated basis is 1,000,000 kWh per year, including supply, transmission, distribution, taxes and fees; consult each record for exceptions. USD values are as supplied; exchange-rate dates are unspecified. Prices, energy consumption, and trade refer to different periods. EJ means exajoules; TWh means terawatt-hours. No country-average price is presented as a global average.

Generation versus primary energy

Electricity shares measure domestic generation, not installed capacity or electricity consumed. Primary energy includes transport and heating and uses substitution accounting; traditional biomass is excluded. Do not multiply these consumption shares by domestic energy production totals: the accounting methods differ. “Other” includes nuclear and other renewables and cannot all be counted as renewable. Electricity oil and other fossil is not a pure-oil estimate. Shares are supplied rounded to two decimals.

Trade & the cost–composition comparison

Net imports equal gross imports minus gross exports. Negative values indicate net exports, not proof of energy independence. Production may be exported; gross flows measure cross-border trade. IEA energy balances use a different accounting method from the primary energy mix. Electricity volumes use EIA data and may differ from generation totals underlying the mix. Electricity imports and exports are preliminary. Scatter-plot fossil share sums coal, gas, and oil/other fossil generation; it is neither emissions intensity nor evidence that the generation mix causes prices. Bubble area is proportional to domestic generation.
